vedic_reference.note: Rooted in the Vedas, specifically the Upanishads, Vedanta is a philosophical concept that explores the nature of reality, the ultimate truth or the ultimate goal of human life.

data.cultural_impact: The term Vedanta is deeply rooted in Hinduism and is known as one of the most influential philosophical traditions of the Hindu spiritual and religious thought. It is associated with the Upanishads, the oldest extant texts of Hinduism, which serve as the foundational texts for the Vedanta philosophical system. This tradition emphasizes the non-dualistic concept of Brahman, the ultimate reality as being all pervasive, sacred, and eternal. Vedanta also encompasses various other philosophical and spiritual teachings in Hinduism, such as the Bhagavad Gita and the works of various Hindu philosophers.
data.spiritual_significance: Vedant is a name that carries immense spiritual significance as it represents the one who has attained the ultimate knowledge and understanding of the universe and the self. In Hinduism, this ultimate knowledge is known as 'Brahma Gyan', the knowledge of the self as the supreme reality of the universe. The name Vedant serves as a constant reminder of the spiritual journey towards self-realization and the ultimate truth of the universe. It also symbolizes wisdom, understanding, and enlightenment.
